summary: Federal agencies must provide risk-commensurate information security protections, NIST standards, continuous monitoring and incident reporting to CISA.
applies_to: Federal agencies and contractors operating federal information systems. It does not directly bind state/local governments.

summary: Safeguard Federal Tax Information: NIST SP 800-53-based controls, Safeguard Security Report, IRS Office of Safeguards reviews, and 24-hour incident reporting.
applies_to: Federal, state and local agencies and their contractors that receive FTI (e.g., revenue, child support, Medicaid/SNAP eligibility, workforce agencies).
status: Rev. 11-2021 is the edition served at irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p1075.pdf as of 2026-09-25.

citation: CJISSECPOL v6.1 (06/25/2026), approved by the CJIS Advisory Policy Board; access tied to 28 CFR Part 20 and user agreements
summary: Minimum security requirements (modernized to a NIST SP 800-53 structure) for creating, viewing, modifying, transmitting, storing and destroying Criminal Justice Information (CJI).
applies_to: Every criminal justice and noncriminal justice agency, contractor or private entity with access to CJI or systems that process it (police, sheriffs, 911/PSAPs with CJI access, courts, corrections, and their vendors).
size_thresholds: No size threshold. Since Oct 1, 2024, audits sanction pre-modernization ('existing') requirements plus [Priority 1] requirements; other priorities phase in.
status: Current version v6.1 dated 06/25/2026 (supersedes v6.0 of 12/27/2024).

citation: Help America Vote Act (52 U.S.C. 20971); VVSG 2.0 (adopted Feb 10, 2021)
summary: Functional, accessibility and security requirements against which voting systems are tested and certified by EAC-accredited labs.
applies_to: Voting system manufacturers; state/local election officials procuring systems.
size_thresholds: Voluntary federally, but mandatory in some states by state law.
status: VVSG 2.0 in effect; EAC stopped certifying to VVSG 1.0/1.1 as of Nov 16, 2023.

summary: See n61: disclosure controls and 'reasonable methods' access controls for education records.
Would require covered entities to report covered cyber incidents to CISA within 72 hours and ransom payments within 24 hours (proposed 226.5).
applies_to: Proposed 226.2(b)(8) SLTT entities (50,000+ population) and (b)(9) education facilities (LEAs with 1,000+ students; Title IV IHEs).
size_thresholds: Population of 50,000 or more (SLTT); 1,000 or more students (LEA/ESA/SEA).
status: PROPOSED ONLY. NPRM 89 FR 23644 (Apr 4, 2024). CISA held town halls (Feb 13 and May 26, 2026 notices) to refine scope. Fall 2025 Unified Agenda targeted a final rule for 09/2026. As of 2026-09-25 no final rule is in the Federal Register; CISA says it 'continues to work on the final rule.' Reporting is not yet mandatory.

short_name: State and Local Cybersecurity Grant Program (SLCGP)
summary: Grant recipients must submit a Cybersecurity Plan with required elements (e.g., asset inventory, monitoring, patching, MFA, workforce, continuity) reviewed by CISA/FEMA; pass-through to local governments.
applies_to: States, territories and Tribal governments (and their local sub-recipients) accepting SLCGP funds.
status: Appropriations authorized FY2022-FY2025 per the U.S. Code text; reauthorization and FY2026+ funding status NOT verified (the FEMA page returned HTTP 403).

citation: GovRAMP program (nonprofit membership organization; NOT law)
summary: NIST SP 800-53-based security verification for cloud providers serving state and local governments. Mandatory only where a state/local procurement policy requires it.
applies_to: Cloud/SaaS vendors to SLTT governments; participating governments.
size_thresholds: Tiered verification (Core, Ready, Provisional/Authorized); Snapshot programs for progressing vendors.
status: Active; stateramp.org now redirects to govramp.org.
